subject: Home range estimates are biologically unreasonable using ctmm.select

messages.author: 6a26b2d9ba78b9a1
messages.subject: Home range estimates are biologically unreasonable using ctmm.select
parts:
Hi everyone,

I'm using ctmm to estimate individual breeding season 95% akdes using ctmm.select. There were three types of GPS units used on my project, so the amount of points varied between 2-6 locations/day, depending on what unit the bird was marked with. Half of the home ranges came out with an order bias <0.01, and the other half came out with an order bias >0.01. Most of these were from units that collected 5-6 locations/day, but there were also a few from the units that collected 2-3 locations/day.  I've started to bootstrap those home ranges with a bias of >0.01, and the estimates I'm getting back are biologically unreasonable. My birds do not have breeding season home ranges >250 km^2, and a couple of the estimates have come back >2,000 km^2 (that is larger than my study area). 

Here is some example code:

Without bootstrapping:
 BU4292g = ctmm.guess(BU4292, interactive=FALSE)

BU4292_pHREML = ctmm.select(BU4292, BU4292g, method="pHREML")

BU4292_UDw = akde(BU4292, BU4292_pHREML, weights = TRUE)

1/summary(BU4292_pHREML)$DOF['area']^2
#area
#0.4244732

summary(BU4292_UDw)
$DOF area bandwidth 1.534742 1.711735 $CI low est high area (square kilometers) 125.9015 1669.847 5155.987

With bootstrapping:

BU4292_BOOT <- ctmm.boot(BU4292, BU4292_pHREML, iterate=FALSE, error=0.05, trace = 1)

1/summary(BU4292_BOOT)$DOF['area']^3 
#area
#3.355178e-05 

BU4292_UDwB = akde(BU4292, BU4292_BOOT, weights=TRUE)

summary(BU4292_UDwB)
#$DOF
#area bandwidth
#31.00474   1.27423
#
#$CI
#                                                       low      est    high
#area (square kilometers) 2821.545 4152.545 5736.66

I'm unclear as to why these estimates are so high. I'm using a weighted AKDE because some of the data had an irregular schedule, particularly when the birds were nesting, and the units did not receive adequate sunlight/clear skies for satellites. The best movement model selected for all of the birds is OUF anisotropic.

Any help is greatly appreciated. Thank you!

Terrah

messages.subject: Re: [ctmm-user] Home range estimates are biologically unreasonable using ctmm.select
parts:
Hi Terrah,

I don't think this individual is range-resident. When the DOF for area is less than 2, it's just not really possible to get a good range estimate. What do the variograms look like?

Jesse

messages.author: 6a26b2d9ba78b9a1
messages.subject: Re: [ctmm-user] Home range estimates are biologically unreasonable using ctmm.select
parts:
Hi Jesse,

Thank you for the quick response. I looked at the variograms, and the birds I'm having issues with definitely were not residents during this time period. All of them also have DOF <2. It looks like I  was capturing movement onto late summer habitat. I adjusted my time period, and everything is running great now! 

Thank you again!
Terrah
